alt: Horizontal bars of scores out of 100 in one run of the original checker: the unchanged starter code, 0; returns an error on RGBA to RGB24, 5.39; returns an error on 3:1 shrink, 18.93; writes nothing on 3:1 shrink, 17.87; all four pass 30 of 30 correctness tests. A note says an error was timed as a 16,469 times speedup. A box describes the current fix and its one side-by-side run: a submission that skips repeated calls passed 30 of 30 correctness tests and scored 0, and a correct submission still scored.
caption: Speed tests that never checked their output let unfinished code earn up to 18.93 of 100 points. The agent rewrites FFmpeg's image-scaling library and is scored on speed once 30 correctness tests pass. The checker never inspected the results of the timed calls, so a call that returned an error or wrote nothing counted as thousands of times faster. In one run of the original checker, three one-line unfinished versions scored 5.39, 18.93 and 17.87, against 0 for the unchanged starter, and all four passed the 30 correctness tests. The current fix checks the output of every timed call and, as the instructions say, sets the whole score to exactly 0 when any call fails. In its one side-by-side run, code that skips repeated calls passed all 30 correctness tests and scored 0.
